analysis.title: Smurfit Westrock (SW): 3Q26 Numbers Miss and Lower 2026 Guidance; Still Constructive Outlook for 2027
key_insights: SW reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $1,205mn, 7% below Visible Alpha consensus of $1,296mn, on weaker North America results where freight and raw material cost inflation hit margins.
GS calls it a weak print. The main negatives were continued volume declines in North America despite a low comparison base, and slower-than-expected price recognition in Europe.
Management lowered FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance to ~$4.7bn from $4.9-5.1bn (Visible Alpha consensus $4.9bn). This implies 4Q adj. EBITDA of ~$1.3bn vs consensus of $1.4bn, about 7% lower.
GS expects low-to-mid-single-digit negative earnings revisions ahead, all else equal, and expects the shares to trade down on the miss and lower guidance.
The 2026 energy and freight cost impact is now guided at $700mn, up from $520mn at 2Q26. GS says this implies a c.$50/t cost increase since the conflict in the Middle East began.
Positives: management said containerboard and consumer board systems in North America remain sold out, and expects a full price pass-through to boxes in Europe in 1H27.

GS believes the still-rising cost backdrop could lead to further paper price hikes. Once costs stabilize and paper prices pass through to boxes, GS expects earnings to pick up materially, especially in North America, in 2027.
Europe, MEA and APAC adj. EBITDA was $379mn, 6% below consensus, on sales of $2,824mn (2% below). Margin was 13.4%, 60bps below consensus.
North America adj. EBITDA was $720mn per the text (-7% vs consensus), with a 16.0% margin, 100bps below consensus. Sales were lower than expected. The Exhibit 2 table shows NA EBITDA of $760mn.
LatAm adj. EBITDA was $126mn, slightly ahead of consensus, on revenue of $587mn with a 21.5% margin in line with consensus.

Cash from operations was $874mn, down ~20% y/y. Cash conversion (CFO/EBITDA) was 73% vs 87% a year ago. Capex was $514mn vs consensus of $656mn. Net debt was $13.3bn, with net debt/EBITDA at 2.9x, unchanged from 2Q26.
FY26 capex guidance was cut to ~$2.3bn from $2.4-2.5bn. SW shares have performed in line with pulp and paper peers over the last month and are up 15% ytd relative to peers.

market_movers.rationale: GS stays Buy with a $53 12-month target (24.6% upside from $42.54) despite the 3Q26 miss and guidance cut. It sees 2027 earnings recovering once costs stabilize and paper price increases pass through to boxes.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term cost inflation and weak North America volumes pressure margins. Sold-out containerboard systems and expected price pass-through support a 2027 recovery.

earnings_insights: SW 3Q26 adj. EBITDA reported $1,205mn vs Visible Alpha consensus $1,296mn (-7.0%) and GSe $1,296mn; down 7.5% y/y from $1,302mn in 3Q25, up 5.7% q/q.
SW 3Q26 adj. EBITDA margin reported 14.8% vs consensus 15.7% (-90bps) and 16.3% in 3Q25.
SW 3Q26 reported EPS $0.42 vs consensus $0.56 (-25.0%) and GSe $0.29; reported net profit $222mn vs consensus $314mn. Reported EBIT $487mn vs consensus $599mn (-18.7%).
SW 3Q26 total revenue reported $8,161mn vs consensus $8,271mn (-1.3%).
SW FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance lowered to ~$4.7bn (from $4.9-5.1bn) vs Visible Alpha consensus of $4.9bn, implying 4Q26 adj. EBITDA of ~$1.3bn vs consensus of ~$1.4bn.
SW 3Q26 free cash flow was $360mn vs consensus $314mn, helped by capex of $514mn vs consensus $656mn.
GS forecasts: FY26E EPS $2.11, FY27E EPS $3.52, FY28E EPS $3.66. FY26E EBIT $2,352mn and FY27E EBIT $3,338mn. Quarterly GS EPS: 9/26E $0.59, 12/26E $0.77, 3/27E $0.72.

tension_points.bull_case: North America containerboard and consumer board systems remain sold out, and management expects full price pass-through to boxes in Europe in 1H27. Further paper price hikes could follow the rising costs, and GS expects earnings to pick up materially once costs stabilize.
tension_points.bear_case: 3Q26 missed by 7%, North America volumes are still declining despite a low comparison base, and Europe price recognition is slower than expected. Energy and freight cost headwinds rose to $700mn, and GS expects negative earnings revisions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further significant volume adjustments in North America, or US tariffs not producing the higher margins GS anticipates, would undermine the thesis.

theme_stances.key_argument: Rising costs could lead to further paper price hikes, and earnings should pick up materially in 2027 once costs stabilize and paper prices pass through to boxes.
